qualifying_items.title: LiteLLM supply-chain impact update maps exposure across thousands of organizations

visible_dates.basis: visible byline timestamp; qualifies inside the cutoff window
date-only primary research page; supporting source, not sole qualification because it is boundary-date without a visible time
visible byline date; supporting in-window secondary source

qualifying_items.evidence_classification: public incident impact update; AI infrastructure supply-chain compromise; credential-exposure assessment
qualifying_items.concise_factual_summary: SecurityWeek's August 12 update reports CloudSEK's assessment that the March LiteLLM package compromise potentially exposed more than 2,500 organizations and more than 430,000 CI/CD pipelines. The malicious LiteLLM versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were tied to the broader Trivy/TeamPCP supply-chain campaign and included credential-stealing behavior. LiteLLM's own advisory says the compromised PyPI packages were live on March 24, 2026 for about 40 minutes, with a broader suspect install window through 16:00 UTC, and recommends checking installs and rotating exposed secrets.

affected_boundary_or_version.affected_window: 2026-03-24T10:39:00Z through about 40 minutes for package availability; LiteLLM advises treating installs through 2026-03-24T16:00:00Z as suspect
affected_boundary_or_version.credential_boundary: environment variables, SSH keys, cloud credentials, Kubernetes tokens, database passwords, CI/CD secrets, publishing tokens, and model provider API keys available to affected processes

qualifying_items.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: LiteLLM is an AI gateway and orchestration dependency that may be installed directly or transitively by AI agent frameworks, MCP servers, and LLM orchestration tools. The incident turns ordinary dependency resolution and CI/CD automation into a model-provider credential and AI-infrastructure exposure path.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad LiteLLM, BerriAI, CloudSEK, Trivy, PyPI, OpenAI, and Anthropic entity context belongs upstream.
General dependency pinning, CI/CD secret rotation, and agent framework transitive-dependency governance belong upstream as development practice.
Retain the security-specific incident lesson: AI infrastructure dependencies and gateway packages need credential rotation, package provenance gates, and transitive install exposure checks.

qualifying_items.confidence_notes: High confidence that the August 12 SecurityWeek item is inside the window and that the affected versions and payload classes are supported by LiteLLM's own advisory. CloudSEK's organization-scale dataset is treated as potential exposure, not confirmed compromise, matching the source caveat.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, reconcile this update with the existing LiteLLM supply-chain secret exposure page if present.
Preserve the distinction between potential exposure counts and confirmed victim compromise.
Check whether upstream ai-wiki already owns durable LiteLLM and CloudSEK entity leaves before creating local references.

qualifying_items.title: CVE-2026-73498 discloses MCP Atlassian arbitrary file read through Confluence attachment upload

visible_dates.basis: CVE metadata datePublished; qualifies inside the cutoff window
CVE metadata dateUpdated; confirms in-window enrichment
NVD published date displayed as 08/12/2026; NVD change history also records August 13 modification

qualifying_items.evidence_classification: public vulnerability advisory; MCP server file-read and credential-exfiltration risk; patch available
qualifying_items.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-73498 says mcp-atlassian versions before 0.22.0 pass a client-supplied file_path into confluence_upload_attachment without validate_safe_path. An authenticated MCP client can read files accessible to the server process and upload them to Confluence. The CVE description explicitly notes that an AI agent induced by untrusted content to call the tool could disclose server environment variables, including CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN and other credentials. Version 0.22.0 fixes the issue.
qualifying_items.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP servers often bridge agent instructions to privileged local files and SaaS APIs. This advisory shows how a normal authenticated tool call can become an agent-mediated credential disclosure when untrusted content steers an agent toward a vulnerable MCP tool.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad Atlassian, Confluence, Jira, and MCP server catalog context belongs upstream.
General MCP server selection and development workflow guidance belongs upstream unless security-specific.
Retain the local security lens for MCP tool file containment, least privilege, credential exposure, and prompt-injection-to-tool-call risk.

qualifying_items.confidence_notes: High confidence because the CVE metadata has precise in-window publication and update timestamps and NVD exposes the vulnerability description, affected version, CVSS, references, and CISA ADP enrichment.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, check whether an MCP Atlassian local security leaf already exists or whether this belongs under agent-and-tool-security or identity-and-access.
Link to upstream MCP server entity coverage rather than duplicating broad product background.
Record that the patch boundary is mcp-atlassian 0.22.0.

qualifying_items.title: GhostJacking update describes poisoned telemetry as an agent takeover path

visible_dates.basis: Tenet page shows 'Latest update: Aug 13th, 2026'; qualifies as visibly updated inside the cutoff window
visible publication date; corroborating in-window secondary security analysis
visible bulletin date; corroborating in-window secondary coverage

qualifying_items.evidence_classification: security research update; agentic kill-chain demonstration; telemetry prompt-injection and delegated-authority risk
qualifying_items.concise_factual_summary: Tenet's updated GhostJacking research describes attacks where poisoned logs or alerts from Cloudflare, Datadog, or Sentry are read by AI agents that also have write-capable tools. The researchers report a chain that can move from initial access through poisoned telemetry to escalation, exfiltration, and persistence, including a remediated Claude Desktop sandbox escape. IANS and The Hacker News summarize the same risk as agents treating operational telemetry as trusted instructions and using their authorized privileges to take unauthorized actions.

platform_boundaries: Cloudflare firewall event logs queried by agent sessions that also hold Cloudflare write/API tools
Datadog and Sentry telemetry or alert data consumed by agents with operational authority
Claude Desktop sandbox escape reported to Anthropic and fixed before the DEFCON presentation
affected_boundary_or_version.not_a_single_cve: Research describes a composition of poisoned telemetry, agent trust, delegated authority, tool scope, sandbox exfiltration, and persistent agent configuration rather than one product CVE.

qualifying_items.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The research reframes security logs, alerts, tickets, and other operational records as attacker-writable instruction channels when agents can both read telemetry and mutate infrastructure. It supports local controls for trust labels, read/write separation, human approval for high-impact actions, and least-privilege agent identities.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad Cloudflare, Datadog, Sentry, Anthropic, and Claude Desktop entity context belongs upstream.
General coding-agent workflow governance and telemetry-driven automation practice belong upstream.
Retain the local security lens for poisoned telemetry, prompt injection, delegated authority, agent identity, approval gates, and runtime monitoring.

qualifying_items.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence. The primary Tenet page is visibly updated August 13 and includes concrete technical claims, but some scale estimates are research extrapolations rather than breach counts. Treat the Claude Desktop sandbox note as reported fixed by the researcher unless corroborated by an Anthropic advisory during ingest.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, consider whether this updates the existing GhostJacking or agentic-browser/telemetry trust pages.
Preserve the distinction between demonstrated vulnerable setups and confirmed breached organizations.
Look for an Anthropic primary confirmation before making durable claims about the sandbox fix beyond Tenet's report.
